Risk Management Program  Data Elements
Simplot Hedges Warehouse

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

For further information concerning this executive summary or other elements of the Risk Management Program please contact Jim Pittam, Terminal Manager at: 

Simplot Hedges Warehouse
227120 E. Hedges Road
Kennewick, WA 99337-7111

Phone: (541) 314-8553

Policies and Guidelines

It is the policy of the Simplot Company (Environmental Policy Statement EN01.1) to manufacture, handle, store and dispose of all substances safely and in compliance with the requirements of federal, state and local environmental laws while reducing the risks to human health, safety and the environment.  Each manager/supervisor is expected to responsibly implement this policy, and each employee is expected to comply fully with the spirit, as well as the letter of this policy.  The Company will assure that the environmental, health and safety laws, regulations, and standards applicable to its products and operations are know and obeyed by employees. 

The Simplot Company Guideline (Safety & Health Policy SA 001) states that the Company is committed to reducing incidents or occurrences in the workplace that result in human injury, illness, or death, and/or destruction or loss to the corporations assets and to be in compliance with all laws and regulations governing workplace safety.  This guideline applies to all groups and separate operating entities of the Simplot Company.  Emergency plans shall be developed for each operating unit outlining the practices and procedures for emergency medical care, fire response, evacuation, or other emergencies.  Each group shall develop and implement appropriate programs for initial and ongoing safety and loss prevention training of employees. 

Regulated Substance(s)

The regulated substance that is episodically stored at this facility would be Anhydrous Ammonia in a railcar at or above the threshold level for the RMP.  Anhydrous Ammonia is received and stored in the railcar

until blended.  The blended material is then stored and distributed as a non-hazardous, non-regulated fertilizer used in crop production. 

Accidental Release Program

This Anhydrous Ammonia facility has implemented the provisions of the State of Washington Administrative Rules for Anhydrous Ammonia and the Safety Requirements for the Storage and Handling of Anhydrous Ammonia as published by the Compressed Gas Association (G-2.1), and the standards of the U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Administration for storage and handling of Anhydrous Ammonia (29 CFR 1910.111).  

Five Year Accident History

In the past five years there have been no accident releases at this site. 

Emergency Response Program

This facility has developed a written emergency contingency plan (Integrated Contingency Plan).  The plan addresses the regulations concerning emergency plans as mandated under: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.38, 1910.119, and 1910.120; EPA 40 CFR 264 subpart D, 265 subpart D, 68 and 279.52; DOT/RSPA-FRP 49 CFR 194.  Elements within this plan include employee training, SARA Title III reporting requirements and community right to know, pre-emergency planning, and emergency response planning. 

Program Ownership and Responsibility

The Simplot Company is the owner and responsible party for implementation and maintenance of the Risk Management Program according to 40 CFR 68; including all elements required withing Program Level 2 guidelines outline in 40 CFR 68.170. 

The contracted mobile pipe reactor company is the owner and responsible party for implementation and maintenance of the Process Safety Management Program guidelines outlined in 29 CFR 1910.119. 

Planned Changes to Improve Safety

Safety and Environmental programs are very dynamic, since this is an ongoing process, changes toward improvement are evaluated and implemented periodically.  The need for improvement is identified by facility employee inputs, inspections and audits which are performed regularly at this facility
